title: The tutorial in six chapters: the SKIP TUTORIAL button becomes a card that shows where the run is (TUTORIAL n/6) with NEXT to the next chapter's start and SKIP ALL, and every chapter is a URL built at boot as a run has it there
context: Owner's second playtest (b8e560d, 2026-09-25): "4) Tutorial. Skip tutorial should have 2 options. 1) Showing 1/x in tutorial, where we are, skip to next phase. 2) skip entire tutorial. it will make it easier to troubleshoot the tutorial and more user-friendly." Before, the opening had one button, SKIP TUTORIAL, a link to ?skip=defence that disappeared at the handover. Nothing showed which part of the opening was playing. The only mid-tutorial entries were developer ones: the drawer's ROTOR (the whole opening), GUNSHIP and DEFENSE (static stage 6), with QUIVER and STUDY unwired, and ?phase=X on a growing page gave inconsistent worlds. ?phase=foundry never deployed the foundry. ?phase=cleared had no Rotor and no gate. ?phase=construction had no gunship, and its first wave came on the first frame. The views strip unlocked about 72 s early. Every late-start page showed the intact rocket. The owner was not asked the three open design choices (he is away; the session's instruction was to continue). Chosen: six chapters, not five (the first wave has its own chapter because it is the part that broke in his playtest); SKIP ALL stays today's back door; and the STÅLHEART chapter starts with the print half done, as a run has it.
outcome: The chapters live in src/content/story-defaults.js (STORY_CHAPTERS, beside STORY_SKIP): LANDING (the landing and the close-up), ROTOR (the foundry, the Rotor's print, the gate), FIRST WAVE (tremor to the fifty cleared, in the Rotor's seat), QUIVER (the hard cores), STÅLHEART (sector 0) and EXPEDITION (the new hull, the study, the landing sites). STORY_CHAPTER_END is sector 1 on the grown base. Each chapter lists its beats (phases), where its page starts (from), the programme steps that stand (printed), the sentries on their sockets (towers), a print already under way (head: the Stålheart a third done at QUIVER and half at STÅLHEART, matching --pacing's timeline) and the rocket sections the AFR-01 has already cut (foundry). ?skip=<chapter> (src/platform/story-world.js readStoryQuery) opens a growing base at stage 1 with the beats at the chapter's start and the full threat. src/core/story-route.js chapterUrl builds that URL and keeps the harness keys; any ?skip= now marks the story route, so a chapter link from an ?acceptance=1 page stays the story. At boot, src/fx/story-entry.js openStoryAt prints the steps through the same storyApi.printed a finished print calls, places the towers as a finished order does, and makes the Stålheart's door every berth past the hull's issue. It also took over SKIP TUTORIAL's boot block from the controller. The beats (src/domain/story-beats.js) now do once, on a late start, what they do on the way in: the foundry is deployed off camera with foundryCut sections cut (src/domain/foundry.js skipFoundry, silent); the views strip is offered only from the first wave's clear; sector 0 calls the gunship, puts the player in the Quiver's optic (where the hard cores left them) and holds its first wave for `first`; the new hull has the construction's study delay. A Quiver that already stands is neither introduced nor ordered at the clear. Isao's order carries head, and his print starts at that share (programme-host, td-tab's worker). The arrival (src/fx/arrival.js `past`) puts the salvage and the foundry in place of the rocket as each loads on any stage-1 page past the landing. The card (src/fx/tutorial-card.js, replacing src/fx/skip-tutorial.js; the id stays #skip-tutorial) shows TUTORIAL n/6, the chapter's name and a pip per chapter, with NEXT › <next chapter> and SKIP ALL. On a phone it is one status line and two 44 px buttons ending above the coach at 268 px. It stays until sector 1 on a growing page (until the handover on a static one). The landing's NEXT ends the landing in the page, which is exactly ROTOR's start, and lets go of the focus so a later Space cannot press it again; while no landing plays it is the ROTOR link; every other NEXT is a link; the last is SECTOR 1. The game's shot skip ignores a press on the card (td-tab shotSkipTap), so NEXT over the landing advances one chapter, not two. The drawer's QUIVER and STUDY jumps are the quiver and expedition chapter URLs. The controller's share costs nothing net: SKIP TUTORIAL's boot block moved out with it (td-tab on the chapters branch 9,436 lines, 536,474 bytes, 17 long lines; with the Rotor tracer fix merged, 9,417, 536,282 and 16, budgets lowered).
alternatives: An in-page NEXT that jumps the beats forward: the beats have no seek (their phase is private and their side effects happen once, on the transitions), Isao's programme prints strictly in order, shots freeze the beats, and in-page restart cleanup is still open work. The project's rule is that route changes reload. A reload builds each chapter from a URL that can be bookmarked and tested, which is the troubleshooting the owner asked for.

Five chapters, ROTOR running from the foundry to the fifty cleared: 70 s, 40 of them watching Isao build before the wave. The first wave is where the owner saw nothing to shoot at, so it gets its own chapter and URL.

The n/6 in the objectives panel: on a phone outside build mode the panel's rows are hidden, the whole panel is hidden during the landing, it repaints only on events, and the owner's open complaint is a cluttered phone HUD. The card already stood over the landing.
SKIP ALL to sector 1 on the grown base: that is where the last chapter's NEXT goes now; SKIP ALL keeps the entry the owner chose on 2026-09-16, straight into the back door with two towers earned.
evidence: Unit tests: test/story-beats.mjs (each chapter start: ROTOR's first barrel orders the Rotor with no views; FIRST WAVE orders the Quiver first and the tremor follows with two sections cut; QUIVER neither introduces nor orders a standing Quiver and hands its optic over; STÅLHEART calls the gunship once, seats the Quiver and holds its first wave; EXPEDITION waits the construction's study delay), test/foundry.mjs (skipFoundry: none, two, all cut; silent; never rewinds a deployed foundry), test/story-query.mjs (every chapter URL opens its start; the chapters cover every beat once, in order; chapterAt), test/story-route.mjs (chapterUrl keeps the harness keys; a chapter link from an acceptance page is the story), test/arrival.mjs (past: no shot, no line, the swap as each landmark loads), test/programme-host.mjs (the head start on the Stålheart's order only).

Browser --chapters (new): the bare page shows 1/6 LANDING over the landing, and NEXT ends it in the page (same URL, the swap, beats at foundry, 2/6 ROTOR, the focus let go). NEXT reloads to ?skip=wave with the harness keys: gate built, Rotor standing, two sections cut, 3/6, and the wave rises with fodder alive. ?skip=quiver: both sentries, the hard core and the optic, the Stålheart print a third done. ?skip=stalheart: the hull held, the gunship on station, the Quiver's optic, the first construction wave, the print half done. ?skip=expedition: the Stålheart and pad standing, the hull out with the door as every berth, the study close-up. NEXT › SECTOR 1: sector 1 opens and the card is gone. --skip-tutorial and --phone updated for the two buttons.
